analysis_steps.goal: Calibrate and image continuum and line cubes

method.value: CASA calibration, tclean continuum and cube imaging with briggs weighting (robust 0.5), hogbom, self-calibration from continuum applied to cubes, pblimit 0.2

evidence.quote: Continuum imaging and line cubes were generated with the TCLEAN task in CASA 5.3.
The self-calibration solutions derived from the continuum images were applied to the line cubes.
The deconvolution was performed using the “hogbom” algorithm with a weighting parameter of “briggs,” and the robust parameter was set to 0.5 to balance sensitivity and resolution.
Primary beam correction was applied using pblimit = 0.2.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit LTE synthetic spectra per core to get T, N for each molecule

method.value: Extract a single-pixel spectrum at each core continuum peak and fit LTE models with XCLASS; CH3OH is handled through 13CH3OH and a 12C/13C ratio

evidence.quote: Spectra were extracted from a single pixel at the continuum peak position of the dense core and averaged over the beam.
Under the assumption of local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), XCLASS solves the radiative transfer equation and generates synthetic spectra for specific molecular transitions

evidence.loc: 3.3 Rotation temperatures, column densities, and abundances
evidence.quote: Considering the errors, the average temperatures of the three molecules are comparable.

claims.hypothesis: CH3COCH3, CH3CHO and CH3OH originate from the same gas via grain-surface chemistry
claims.experiment: Combined morphology and abundance correlations with Garrod et al. 2022 warm-up model predictions
claims.result: Mean abundance 6.2e-8 is comparable to the slow-warm-up prediction of 1.4e-8; no model links CH3COCH3 and C2H5CN
claims.finding: The three O-bearing molecules likely share a grain-surface origin; C2H5CN may only coexist

evidence.quote: The average abundance of CH$_{3}$COCH$_{3}$ is (6.2$\pm$1.3)$\times$10$^{-8}$, which is comparable to the slow timescale model prediction.
However, no chemical models suggest a direct association between CH$_{3}$COCH$_{3}$ and C$_{2}$H$_{5}$CN.

claims.hypothesis: Acetone in H, I and L cores resembles that in high-, intermediate- and low-mass star-forming regions
claims.experiment: Compared mean T, N and abundance by core class with published values
claims.result: H-core mean T 134 K, N 4.2e16 cm^-2; I-core N 7.9e15; L-core N 1.6e15
claims.finding: Emitting gas may have similar conditions to that in the respective literature regimes

evidence.quote: These comparisons suggest that the CH$_{3}$COCH$_{3}$ emitting gas in the H, I, and L cores may have similar physical and chemical conditions

why_this_data.value: Earlier acetone work was limited to single targets or small single-dish samples, so a larger interferometric sample with matched resolution and spectral setup was needed

evidence.quote: comprehensive interferometric studies targeting CH$_{3}$COCH$_{3}$ and chemically associated molecules across a larger sample with a similar angular resolution and spectral setup are essential

why_this_method.value: 13CH3OH is fitted instead of CH3OH because CH3OH lines are optically thick and blended

evidence.quote: Due to the optical thickness and blending of certain CH$_{3}$OH lines (see Appendix [8](#sec:mt)), we fit the isotopolog $^{13}$CH$_{3}$OH as an alternative in the 16 cores.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Fitting CH3OH directly was replaced by fitting 13CH3OH because of optical depth and blending

evidence.quote: we fit the isotopolog $^{13}$CH$_{3}$OH as an alternative in the 16 cores

limitations_admitted.value: Source size from the continuum may underestimate the line-emitting size and so overestimate fitted column densities

evidence.quote: This may lead to an underestimation of the source size, resulting in an overestimate of the fitted column densities.

limitations_admitted.value: Poor continuum sensitivity because fewer than 10% of channels are line-free

evidence.quote: resulting in relatively poor continuum sensitivity

limitations_admitted.value: Resolved scales above 2000 au are too coarse to see the Orion-KL-like differences between molecules

evidence.quote: whereas the resolved linear scales of our samples exceed 2000 au

referee_caveats_inferred: Abundances share the same N(H2) denominator and CH3CHO shares the CH3COCH3 temperature, so the abundance correlations may be partly built in; no test against N(H2) alone is shown
Dust temperature is set equal to the CH3OCHO gas temperature, which directly drives N(H2) and all abundances
LTE with a single temperature and a continuum-based source size is applied to line emission that the authors say is more extended in some cores
The intermediate-mass core count is 3 in the abstract and table but 4 in Section 3.1
Several CH3OH abundance uncertainties in the table exceed the value (for example 3.1 +/- 9.6 e-6), suggesting an error propagation problem
The correlation method (Pearson or rank) and how errors enter it are not described, with only 16 cores of heterogeneous distance (2.7 to 10.1 kpc)

missing_for_reproduction: Core catalogue (positions, sizes, fluxes, T_dust, masses) lives in Chen et al. 2024 and CH3OH columns in Li et al. 2024
Self-calibration parameters and tclean cube settings
XCLASS/MAGIX run configuration (ranges, chain settings, windows, version)
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: About 11 fields in one Band 7 C43-1 project with four SPWs; raw MS likely tens of GB, calibrated data a few tens of GB (inferred, not stated)
reproducibility.score_reason: Score on a 1-5 scale: data source and imaging basics are stated, but core table, CH3OH columns and XCLASS fit configuration depend on other papers or are missing
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The ALMA project code is given, but the core catalogue and CH3OH columns come from other papers and the XCLASS/MAGIX setup and self-calibration are unspecified, so the numeric results cannot be redone from this paper alone

methods_papers.why: XCLASS line identification and LTE fitting
Dense-core extraction, sizes, fluxes, masses and temperatures

companion_papers.why: UC Hii regions traced by H40alpha
Chemical model used for abundance comparison

related_projects_or_surveys: ATOMS (ALMA Three-millimeter Observations of Massive Star-Forming Regions); this Band 7 project is a pilot
